title: Midnight fleet log and strategy sketch — week Dec 6 2027
content:
Context and intent:
This is the working log from the midnight-capacity huddle (hand-off shifted to 22:00 PT for the west coast surge window). Purpose: capture run-of-week observations, short experiments we ran on prewarming and preemption hedging, and sketch tactical changes we want to try next sprint. Not an exec brief — intentionally rough notes and open questions for SRE/Serving/Infra syncs.

Attendees:
- Maya Chen (infra ops) — owner
- Arjun Patel (serving-runtime)
- Louisa Becker (regional capacity)
- Diego Ramirez (SRE oncall)
- Claire Ng (release eng — guest)

High level summary:
- Weekend surge (DEC 4–5) had two ~45m hotspots in eu-west1 where latency SLOs crept to 225ms p50 (target 170ms) due to a simultaneous maintenance evict + bursty PLG onboarding traffic. Autoscale responded but cold-starts and cross-zone data movement spiked p99.
- Prewarming experiment v3 (short lived) reduced cold-start tail by ~38% for A100-backed nodes when warm cache hit reached 55%. Warm cache is not yet reliably maintained for low-traffic tenants.
- Preemption hedging prototype (priority bands + soft-reserve slots) prevented cascading fallback to lower-fidelity models in 3/5 test cases; still failing under multi-region preemption storms.

Quantified metrics (week over week):
- Total cluster GPU-hours consumed (global): 42,900 (up 12% WoW)
- Peak concurrent GPUs used (global): 1,540 (up 220 GPUs)
- p50 latency (production mix): 162ms (target 170ms) — OK
- p95 latency: 420ms (worse in eu regions during evictions)
- Cold-start tail (% requests >1s): 3.4% -> after prewarm v3: 2.1% (A100), H100 baseline unchanged
- Preemption events (cloud spot): 27 events this week, with 9 events clustered in eu-west over 2 windows

What we observed (notes):
- eu-west1 maintenance coincided with a capacity reclaim job that aggressively returned nodes to the autoscaler pool. Timing was bad — nodes became available but with hot KV-cache loss; serving requests experiencing replumbing to new nodes caused p99 injections.
- Customers on Dedicated saw fewer falls to fallback models; our smart-routing rules favored Dedicated-eligible capacity earlier this run (good).
- Edge region LA-A (experimental) showed lower latency variance for short-chat workloads, but throughput jitter was high when prewarming quotas were not filled. LA-A priming needs clearer priming window TTL.
- Node labels and topology hints are inconsistent between fleet-config v2 and v2.1 (PR #214). This causes some allocations to select H100 pools when A100 is acceptable, raising cost.

Short experiments run this week (results + learnings):
1) Prewarm v3 — short-lived ephemeral warmers
- Mechanic: keep small set of ephemeral pods pinned per AZ per model family for 30–60m when we predict a surge.
- Result: cold-start tail improved for A100-backed models but increased idle GPU-hours by ~0.7%.
- Actionable: lower keeper TTL to 20m for low-confidence predictions, add chargeback metric so customers are not silently paying.

2) Priority-band hedging (prototype)
- Mechanic: reserve soft slots per region per priority band; on spot preemption, attempt local failover before routing to other regions.
- Result: prevented model-fidelity fallbacks in majority of single-region preemptions, but multi-region events still cause thrashing due to cross-region capacity coord latency.
- Actionable: investigate gossip-style slot state propagation (lower bound 300ms), and consider ephemeral cross-region burst pools with tighter failback windows.

3) On-demand kernel selection throttle
- Mechanic: limit live kernel selection changes during high-traffic periods to avoid kernel cache churn on node.
- Result: small improvement in p99 latency during hot reconfigs; needs longer run.

Known issues & near-term risks:
- Fleet config drift (v2 vs v2.1 labels) -> cost leakage to H100. Risk: monthly cost delta could grow if not patched before next procurement window.
- Cross-region failover delay is aggravated by our routing-control-plane refresh interval (currently 3s). In high-churn preemption windows this adds seconds of tail.
- Observability gaps: KV-cache eviction metrics not surfaced to Console per-tenant (we only have cluster-level metrics). Hard to correlate latency spikes to cache losses for specific customers.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Maya: bake TTL change for prewarm keepers to 20m, include chargeback meter in cost pipeline. ETA: WIP, rollout canary by 2027-12-10. (INF-4821)
- Arjun: prototype gossip-style slot propagation (poC that reduces cross-region slot latency). ETA: spike 1 week, demo 2027-12-14. (INF-4876)
- Louisa: run cost-impact analysis for label drift (v2.1 auto-upgrade risk) and gate to procurement. ETA: 2027-12-09. (INF-4855)
- Diego: add KV-cache eviction per-tenant counters to telemetry (work with observability). ETA: initial metrics 2027-12-12. (OBS-132)
- Claire: verify fleet-config PR #214 labeling tests and unblock merge. ETA: 48h. (GH-214)

Decisions to make this sprint (open):
- Tighten autoscaler reclaim dwell time during scheduled maint windows? (safety vs cost). Proposal: add maintenance-aware dwell extension (30–90s) for AZs in maintenance.
- Do we accept 0.5% weekly idle GPU-hour increase to gain ~38% cold-start reduction, or prefer finer prediction models?

Notes for downstream teams:
- Serving-runtime: expect short follow-up RFC on gossip propagation pattern and implications for routing deterministic behavior.
- SRE: ensure incident runbook includes new handoff note to check KV-cache warmers state in the first 10m after maint windows.
- Observability: prioritise tenant-level cache eviction metric — this will materially speed triage for latency imputations.

Loose ideas / backlog for exploration (not committed):
- Region-local ephemeral cross-account burst pool (billing-identified) to soak temporary surges without changing long-term allocation.
- Use compact model variants automatically for requests that match deterministic low-cost patterns during constrained windows (bandshift model).
- Experiment with predictive priming using historical 15-min pattern windows for PLG cohorts (ML spike classifier).

Appendix: snippets and references captured during huddle:
- Slack thread: #infra-eu \"eu maintenance tide\" (link pinned in confluence notes)
- Quick grep of kube events log: several \"Evicting pod due to node maintenance\" entries between 02:12–02:20 UTC on Dec 5.
- Quick cost snapshot: H100 transient spend +9% for the week due to mislabelling.

If you read only one thing: we need tenancy-aware cache metrics and to fix the fleet label drift. Those two moves materially reduce triage time and near-term cost leakage.

Maya — 2027-12-06 (draft)

Open questions for next handoff:
- Louisa: do we want to prototype the ephemeral cross-region pool as a managed product feature or internal infra only?
- Arjun: how aggressive should gossip propagation be vs consistency for routing decisions?
- Diego: can we get a beta telemetry stream for per-tenant cache evictions to the console?

End of log.
